1 لَجِبَ , aor.
لَجَبَ , inf. n. لَجَبٌ, It [a number of men] cried out, or vociferated; raised a clamour, or confused noise. (S, K.) See also art. جلب. ―
-b2- لَجِبَ, inf. n. لَجَبٌ, It (a clamour, or confused noise,) rose. (TA.) ―
-b3- لَجِبَ, inf. n. لَجَبٌ, It (the sea) was agitated, or in commotion; its waves conflicting, or dashing together. (K.) ＝
-A2- لَجُبَتْ, aor.
لَجُبَ , (inf. n. لُجُوبَةٌ, TA;) and ↓ لجّبت , inf. n. تَلْجِيبٌ; She (a sheep or goat) had little milk; (S, K:) or her milk dried up, in consequence of her having passed four months since bringing forth. (S.) See لَجْبَةٌ. ＝
-A3- In a trad. respecting Moses and the stone, occur the words, فَلَجَبَهُ ثَلَاثَ لَجَبَاتٍ, which IAth says he cannot
explain, unless the right reading be فَلَحَتَهُ ثلاث لَحَتَاتٍ [And he struck it three blows]. (TA.)
From An Arabic-English Lexicon (Edward William Lane)
